findings.title: TopBar's `user` prop is dead/duplicated against UserBadge's self-fetch — the SDD specifies two contradictory data paths for the same mock user
findings.evidence: component_breakdown.TopBar.props declares `user: shape({ name, role, initials })` and data_flow literally says 'AppShell renders ... TopBar(title=..., user=useCurrentUser())' — i.e. AppShell calls useCurrentUser() and passes the result into TopBar as a prop. But component_breakdown.UserBadge.props is explicitly '(none — self-fetches via useCurrentUser)', and TopBar's own role text says it renders 'UserBadge on the right' with no mention of forwarding a user prop into it. UserBadge takes no props, so TopBar has nowhere to put the `user` prop it receives — it would be unused inside TopBar, and useCurrentUser() would end up called twice (once in AppShell to build the prop, once again inside UserBadge) for the same mock object.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a genuine 'No Unused Code' (CLAUDE.md §1) violation waiting to happen: whichever of stage 3.3/3.5 implements this literally either (a) threads a `user` prop into TopBar that nothing consumes, or (b) has to silently deviate from the SDD to make it consistent, which is exactly the kind of drift this stage exists to catch before code is written. It is also a minor coupling smell — two different data-access strategies (prop-drilling vs. self-fetching hook) for the identical piece of state, with no stated reason for the split.
findings.recommendation: Stage 3.3 (System Engineer) should resolve this one way before 3.5 builds: either (a) drop the `user` prop from TopBar entirely and let TopBar render `<UserBadge />` with no props (UserBadge self-fetches, consistent with its own spec — the simpler option, and the one already implied by UserBadge's props list), or (b) keep TopBar prop-driven and have UserBadge accept a `user` prop instead of calling useCurrentUser() itself. Option (a) is recommended: it matches UserBadge's already-agreed self-fetching design and avoids call-siting useCurrentUser() in two places for one mock value.
findings.blocking_rationale: Not Critical/blocking — this is an internal data-flow inconsistency inside a still-unbuilt SDD, not a rendered-chrome/UX defect like AC-1, and it doesn't compromise the app-shell-vs-marketing separation that was this stage's core adversarial concern. It is flagged with enough detail that stage 3.3 can resolve it without another SDD round-trip.

findings.title: supporting_modules introduces a new src/mock/ top-level directory, deviating from tech-lead's literal 'src/lib/currentUser.js' path without call-out
findings.evidence: tech-lead's stage 2.5 summary states signed-in-user context should be 'one static MOCK_CURRENT_USER object in a new src/lib/currentUser.js'. The SDD instead places it at 'src/mock/currentUser.js' (a directory not present in CLAUDE.md §3's repo file map, which lists only src/components, src/hooks, src/lib under src/) and adds a second file, src/hooks/useCurrentUser.js, as the consuming hook.
findings.why_it_matters: Tech-lead's hard_constraints_for_solution_architect were flagged upstream as things to respect verbatim. This is a silent path deviation, not a documented, justified one (contrast with the SDD's dependency_decision section, which does explicitly flag and justify its one deviation — the prop-types exception). That said, the actual split (data module + a use-prefixed hook, in separate files) matches the codebase's own established idiom more closely than a single combined file would: codebase-explorer's mapping already documents src/lib/masterDataApi.js (data) + src/hooks/useMasterDataTable.js (hook) as the precedent pattern this feature should extend, not replace.
findings.recommendation: Not blocking. Two acceptable resolutions for stage 3.3/3.5: (a) keep the two-file split (it's the better fit for the existing hook-contract convention) but move the mock object into src/lib/currentUser.js instead of inventing a new src/mock/ directory, keeping the data file next to masterDataApi.js as its sibling; or (b) if the owner/tech-lead prefers isolating mock-only fixtures for easy future removal, keep src/mock/ but say so explicitly as a deliberate, named deviation (the same way the prop-types exception was called out) rather than leaving it unflagged. Recommend (a) — no new top-level src/ directory is needed for one file.
